detection_architecture.rationale: Connector recognition requires both image-only geometric evidence (vertex count, aspect, notch structure) and conductor-interaction evidence (crossing count/points), which are available at two different points in the existing pipeline. A new standalone image-stage ConnectorGeometryDetector emits ShapeKind::ConnectorBody regions into the existing ShapeDetectionArtifacts type; a second, later semantic-stage extension (co-located with TerminalLocationDetector/TerminalRecognizer) evaluates conductor-crossing evidence once ConductorSegments exist.

representation.component_model: ComponentCandidate unchanged; ConnectorBody-kind ShapeRegions bypass ComponentCandidate entirely and feed the ConnectorCandidate pipeline directly (avoids adding ComponentCandidateKind::Connector, which would conflate component/connector semantics and require every existing consumer to add a case)
representation.shape_model: New ShapeKind::ConnectorBody value added to the existing 3-value enum {Rectangle, Circle, ChassisGround}; geometry-only, no electrical/pin/wire implication
representation.connector_model: Reuse existing ConnectorCandidate struct (id, component_candidate_id, bounds, confidence, semantic_labels) verbatim, no field changes
representation.terminal_model: Reuse existing ConnectorTerminal and TerminalCandidateKind::ConnectorBoundary verbatim, no field changes; new ConnectorPin struct added as the missing intermediate state between connector-body recognition and terminal-candidate evidence

wire_semantics.notes: Wire remains strictly endpoint-to-endpoint (start_endpoint/end_endpoint, both EndpointCandidate ids). Splice/Junction/Crossing topology nodes are never Wire boundaries (AP-WIRE-029 invariant, unmodified). A ConnectorPin or Resolved ConnectorTerminal existing at a location is necessary context for WireSemanticResolver's existing semantic labeling of an already-decided Wire endpoint, never sufficient cause to create a new Wire boundary. PhysicalWireIdentityReconstructor's topology/ConductorSegment-based boundary decisions are not modified.

electrical_net_semantics.notes: ElectricalNetResolver and ElectricalNet fields are not modified. ONE NET != ONE WIRE and ONE WIRE != ONE NET both preserved. Connector terminal net membership is decided entirely by existing topology/distribution logic once an endpoint exists; no net-membership evidence is manufactured from connector visual adjacency.

design_gates.question: Does the geometry model represent all 12 source-grounded connector families?
Can all 33 visible connector-side pins be represented without conflating them with Wire endpoints?
Can the existing Wire identity semantics remain unchanged?
Can Electrical Net resolution remain unchanged except for legitimate connector-terminal evidence?
Can connector detection avoid the known ground false-positive patterns?
Can the design represent an unresolved connector without guessing?
Is every required model change actually justified?
